name: Luke
whenBasis: From Paul's second journey, dated from the Gallio inscription, to his last letters.
summary: Paul's fellow worker, whom Colossians calls the beloved physician. He sends greetings with Demas to the Colossians and to Philemon, and in Paul's last letter he is the only one with him. Tradition makes him the author of the Gospel of Luke and Acts, both addressed to Theophilus.
body: The letters name him only three times. In parts of Acts the story switches to we, from Troas to Philippi, and from Philippi on to Jerusalem and Rome, as if the writer was with Paul.

later.text: Irenaeus and the Muratorian fragment (late second century) name Luke, Paul's companion, as author of the Gospel and Acts; a prologue of uncertain date adds that he was from Antioch in Syria and died at eighty-four in Boeotia.
Colossians 4:10–14 names Aristarchus, Mark and Jesus Justus as “the only Jews among my fellow workers,” and Luke after them; read so, he was a Gentile.

sources.title: Saint Paul's Epistles to the Colossians and to Philemon
sources.author: J. B. Lightfoot
sources.note: on Philemon 23–24: 'Aristarchus and Mark belonged to the Circumcision (Col. iv. 11), while Demas and Luke were Gentile Christians'
